Figure 1.Motivation for our method in continual learning for long-horizon agents.
Harness- and model-only methods either enable fast experience reuse but tend to plateau, or suffer from instability and forgetting.
HaMo combines both mechanisms to achieve steady improvement within domains and better retention across domain shifts.

Figure 2.Overview of the HaMo framework.
HaMo continuously distills expert trajectories into a persistent harness memory, selects representative anchor trajectories based on retrieval coverage, and combines them with historical replay to update a LoRA adapter through experience-conditioned behavioral cloning. An optional feedback step releases memory entries associated with trained high-quality trajectories after adaptation. This collaboration enables fast experience reuse at the harness level and gradual knowledge internalization at the model level.

Figure 4.Cross-domain continual learning with Qwen3-8B in the order ScienceWorld (S), ALFWorld (A), and WebShop (W). Panels (a)–(c) show performance after each training stage. Bar groups compare methods, and colors indicate evaluation domains. Higher scores are better.
Figure 5.Component ablation on Qwen3-8B with the training order ScienceWorld (S), ALFWorld (A), and WebShop (W). Each group reports performance after training on the indicated dataset.

Figure 6.Training-order ablation on Qwen3-8B. S, A, and W denote ScienceWorld, ALFWorld, and WebShop, respectively. Final-stage total (S+A+W) sums the three dataset scores measured after the final training stage for each training order.
